pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an array and a slice in Go? What three fields make up a slice header?
expected_points: array: fixed length that is part of the type, assignment copies all elements
slice: a small header describing a window onto a backing array
header fields: pointer to an element of the backing array, len, cap

questions.prompt: Given `s := make([]int, 3, 5)` and `t := s[1:3]`: what are len(t) and cap(t)? If you then write `t[0] = 99`, what happens to s?
expected_points: cap(t) = 4 — capacity runs from the pointer to the end of the backing array (cap(s) - lo), not to hi
s[1] becomes 99: slicing shares the backing array, so t aliases s

questions.prompt: Why is `s = append(s, v)` the required shape? What can go wrong if you write `t := append(s, v)` and keep using both t and s?
expected_points: when len == cap, append allocates a bigger array, copies the elements, and returns a header pointing at the new memory
the returned header is the only one guaranteed current — the old s may point at a stale or shared array
whether t and s alias depends on spare capacity, so the bug appears only at certain lengths

questions.prompt: How do you make an independent duplicate of a slice, and why isn't `dst := src` enough?
expected_points: dst := src copies only the header — both slices alias the same backing array
allocate with make([]int, len(src)) then copy(dst, src)
copy transfers min(len(dst), len(src)) elements and never grows dst, so an unsized destination silently copies nothing

questions.prompt: Slice expressions are half-open: s[lo:hi] includes lo but excludes hi. How did that convention help you avoid index bugs in Insert and Remove?
expected_points: length of a range is simply hi - lo
s[:i] and s[i:] partition the slice with no overlap and no off-by-one adjustment
in Remove, s[:i] plus s[i+1:] cleanly skips exactly element i; in Insert, i == len(s) naturally means append

questions.prompt: The famous one-liner `append(s[:i], s[i+1:]...)` removes element i. The exercise tests reject it — why? When would it be the right choice?
expected_points: s[:i] aliases s, so the append shifts elements inside the input's backing array — the caller's slice is visibly modified
the returned slice still aliases the input
it is fine (and efficient) when the caller owns the slice and wants in-place removal — the contract decides
